pages.text: Macromyzon siluricus was a species of very large early leech, recently discovered in Early Silurian deposits of the Brandon Bridge Formation belonging to the world-renowned Waukesha Lagerstätte. During the Silurian, those sediments were a shallow, near-shore carbonate platform in a tropical setting, teeming with invertebrate life exquisitely preserved in the fossils of the lagerstätte.
Contrarily to most modern leeches, which are generally blood-sucking parasites of vertebrates, Macromyzon was likely an invertebrate specialist using as host the various artiopods of its biota.
